### attention/delivery/readme
'The README is the front door, and a stranger gives it one screen: what it is for in a sentence anyone can read, who it is not for, and the shortest real example that shows it working, before any feature list, architecture or history. Then the one command that starts it from a clean machine with versioned prerequisites and the output it should print, its status and limitations, where to report a problem, and the licence; everything else is linked, never inlined. Show rather than assert, per @pictures_first - a screenshot, a short recording, a live demo or a real output, and measured numbers with their conditions instead of adjectives - keep badges to facts that matter, decorate only to route the eye with a logo or banner and an emoji as a section anchor rather than as punctuation, and test every command you print, because an outdated README misleads worse than none. @surface @prose @pictures_first @bootstrap @readme_tested'

### intent
For single-human software/AI engineering and research, quality is defined by the user's intent, and nothing is fixed - only the price of changing it differs. Assume a capable model that can drift, anchor or lose state; make consequential choices and recovery discoverable rather than teaching generic programming.

### intent/roles/main_agent
In discussion (eager mode) the main agent communicates, investigates and directly executes the user's immediate requests, and delegates only with the user's explicit permission or when a large, independently specifiable slice cannot be finished by one script and is big enough to repay a contract, an integration and a second model's drift - in practice twenty or more such files; the PO stays the only voice to the user, and only in the advance phase does the main agent equal delegation. @phases @handoff @model_cost

### resources/work_areas/untrack
'What should never have been tracked comes out in two steps: untrack and ignore it first, which is local and immediately clean, then rewrite the history that still carries it - automatically while no remote branch holds it, and only with his explicit permission once it is published, because a rewrite changes every hash and invalidates every clone. A secret is rotated as well as removed, because a rewrite does not un-leak it. @regeneration_cost @high_risk @secrets'

### resources/work_areas/no_trash
'At a safe point every path is committed, declared or excluded by an owner, never a fourth state: an untracked or unexplained modification is trash, and trash is a defect, because it hides real work, invites a blind add and makes the tree unreadable to the next session. Find out what it is, commit it if it is project content, declare it if it is too large, ignore it only when an owner explains it, and ask when the classes cannot be told apart; never delete it to make the tree look clean. @track_or_ignore @store_or_declare @untrack @preserve_work @safe_point'

### resources/environment/bootstrap
Every kept project returns from a fresh clone with one committed command that rebuilds its environment from a lockfile, and the README states that command, its measured time and what it cannot rebuild. The command is code, so it is exercised on a clean clone instead of remembered, and it says what the clone is missing before the work needs it; a project whose setup cannot be replayed that way is not done, because everything the clone cannot rebuild is either declared or lost. @follow_toolchain @reproduce @store_or_declare @readme_tested

### resources/environment/reproduce
'A result is either a reproduction or an artefact, never hopefully both: a reproduction pins its inputs, versions and seed and reruns to the same bytes, while a non-deterministic or unpinned pipeline gives a different result each time, so its output is an artefact of record, frozen and hashed instead of promised as a rebuild. Keep the smallest sufficient input - source, data snapshot, config, seed, weights - before keeping a large derived output, and store the output itself when it carries the claim. @regeneration_cost @experiment_record @store_or_declare'

### change/shape/chain
The layers form one chain, each judged by the one above, and each layer's facts carry what the layer above cannot - pain the sufferer and the evidence the pain exists, need what must become true, product the behaviour with its quality bar and its non-goals, architecture each module with its interface and its boundary, method how the thing is measured or built with its names, protocols and conventions, plan each work package with its owner, acceptance and budget, result what was measured and what was inferred from it, and code the file with its types, internal interfaces and conventions.

### laws/projection
A graph written as a tree. Physicalise the main direction and priority order of siblings; preserve that order during semantic edits. When the organization is wrong, make a separately inspectable structural move with its rationale and repaired references, then change meaning, so neither diff hides the other. ### laws/no_op
'Admission: keep a rule when omitting it would materially impair orientation, a consequential decision, coordination, error prevention or recovery, even if a capable model already knows the technique. State its trigger and observable action with completion evidence or a failure route; remove exposition that changes none of these. A split earns its place only when its children specialize one subject and change how the reader acts.'

### resources/work_areas/worktree
'Isolate a parallel writer in a git worktree made from main and kept outside that repository''s working tree: git worktree add ../.worktrees/<repo>/<slug> -b <slug> main shares the same .git, needs no bare repository or clone, and keeps the main tree free of a second copy that every recursive search would read and a git clean -xdf would delete. Git''s own bookkeeping in .git/worktrees holds links, never files, and a worktree is derivative: its branch is pushed at every safe point, so moving, copying or backing up the repository need not carry it, and it is removed once the branch lands. When the parent directory is itself a repository, that repository ignores .worktrees/ once. List with git worktree list, and prefer the main area when a repository''s submodules would need re-initialising in each worktree. @main_area @cleanup_check @no_trash'

### resources/environment/regeneration_cost

### resources/environment/regeneration_cost

### attention/delivery/readme

### intent

Assume a capable model that can drift, anchor or lose state; make consequential choices and recovery discoverable rather than teaching generic programming.

### resources/environment/store_or_declare

A second disk or machine reached by rsync is a first-class durable home, because it keeps the exact bytes a rebuild would change and costs one command, and the cloud is for what must leave the machine. An entry that does not verify is a missing file. @absent @keep_evidence @artefacts_home @bootstrap

### laws/self_improvement/strongest_cure
